events.text: Constellation Software listed on the TSX (ticker CSU) on May 17, 2006, an IPO priced at C$17.00 per share that raised about C$80 million; shares closed their first day of trading at C$18.30. The offering reportedly raised no primary capital for the company itself and was structured mainly to give early investor TD Capital Canadian Private Equity Partners a liquidity event.
events.source_title: Constellation Software has delivered a 36,000% return since its IPO. Is it still a buy? - Cantech Letter
events.note: IPO price/date/first-day-close figures came from a synthesized web search answer drawing on multiple pages found in the same search (including this article, stockanalysis.com, and Constellation's own short-form prospectus at https://www.csisoftware.com/docs/default-source/press-releases/csi-final-prospectus-eng.pdf); the exact underlying page stating C$17.00 could not be individually confirmed since page content could not be fetched directly in this environment (WebFetch is disabled). Treat as third_party pending direct confirmation from the prospectus PDF.

events.text: At IPO, Constellation Software management stated a five-year performance objective: to grow, on average, Net Revenues per share and Adjusted EBITDA per share by 20% per annum for the period January 1, 2006 to December 31, 2010. Management noted that screening public companies with over $50 million in revenue for that growth profile over a trailing five years found fewer than 1% qualified, underscoring how ambitious the target was.
events.source_title: Constellation Software Business History - by Speedwell Research
events.note: Whether the 20%-per-annum target was actually met by year end 2010 could not be confirmed in the searches performed; see gaps.

events.text: Mark Leonard's stated capital-allocation hurdle rates for acquisitions have historically run in the 20%-30% range, tiered by deal size: roughly 30% for smaller acquisitions, 25% for mid-sized ones, and a lower rate (around 20%) for larger deals (roughly $100 million and up).
events.source_title: Constellation Software: Competition, Hurdle Rates & Deal Flow - In Practise
events.note: Exact publication date of this interview/article was not confirmed in the search snippet; date field uses an approximate placement based on context clues (references to the 2021 hurdle-rate change) and should be verified against the article's actual publish date.

events.text: In 2021 Mark Leonard lowered Constellation's hurdle rate specifically for large vertical-market-software (VMS) acquisitions while keeping the hurdle rate unchanged for small and medium-sized deals. Leonard's stated reasoning: over the prior five years, brokers had only invited Constellation into about 16% of large VMS sale processes, and a lower hurdle rate for large deals would let competent M&A brokers include Constellation in more auctions and let the company deploy its cash stockpile, without bidding up prices on the small/medium deals where the higher hurdle rate had been preserving returns.
events.source_title: Constellation Software's next step: expansion through larger takeovers - The Globe and Mail
events.note: Corroborated in search summary by Cantech Letter, June 2021, 'I underestimated Constellation Software, this investor says' (https://www.cantechletter.com/2021/06/i-underestimated-constellation-software-this-investor-says/).

events.text: The 2018 President's letter was Mark Leonard's last full annual letter to shareholders. He stated he would no longer write yearly letters as a matter of course, only writing when he believed he had something new and important to communicate. Reported rationale: sharing Constellation's hard-won operating and capital-allocation tactics in public letters was seen as helping an expanding field of 'Constellation emulators' (copycat acquirers), which he judged was no longer in long-term shareholders' interest.
events.source_title: Mark Leonard Stopped Writing to Shareholders in 2018 - Eagle Talon Partners Investment Firm
events.note: A separate search result referenced an earlier (circa 2009-era) quote where Leonard said a given letter would be 'the last quarterly letter' while still planning to write annual letters; that is a distinct, earlier discontinuation of quarterly (not annual) letters and should not be conflated with the 2018 discontinuation of the annual letter.

events.text: On April 4, 2011 Constellation's board announced it was reviewing strategic alternatives to enhance shareholder value (internally called 'The Process' by Mark Leonard, who had flagged the possibility in his 2010 President's letter, describing it as meaning the company was likely to be sold), retaining BofA Merrill Lynch and BMO Capital Markets as advisors. During the roughly nine-month review, operating group managers were told to stop acquiring in new verticals and 2011 acquisition spending came in at less than half of 2010's level; with less capital going into newly acquired, initially unprofitable businesses, reported profit rose sharply. The process concluded without a sale, and Constellation remained a public company.
events.note: The narrative detail on the nine-month process, advisor names, and its conclusion without a sale is corroborated by a third_party source, https://businesscaseweekly.substack.com/p/bcw-49-constellation-software ('BCW 49: Constellation Software' - Business Case Weekly), and by the original strategic-alternatives announcement referenced in search results (title: 'CONSTELLATION SOFTWARE INC. TO EVALUATE STRATEGIC ALTERNATIVES', https://www.csisoftware.com/category/press-releases/2019/01/21/constellation-software-inc.-to-evaluate-strategic-alternatives -- note this URL's 2019 date-path appears to be a site re-indexing artifact for a 2011-dated release; the original release date is 2011, not 2019, and this should be verified directly against the release.

events.text: After the one-time USD 20 special dividend paid in April 2019, Constellation did not declare further special dividends through the rest of the window. The company's stated reasoning for using capital for acquisitions rather than further special dividends centers on its confidence in deploying retained capital at high returns; Mark Leonard has been quoted characterizing dividends as a signal about capital deployment capacity: 'The dividend is clearly a signal about capital deployment. If we thought that we could deploy this capital at high rates of return, we would have kept it.'
events.source_title: Mark Leonard's Constellation Software Inc. (CSI): The Great Serial Acquirer - Excelsior Capital
events.note: This quote and rationale were surfaced via a synthesized search answer combining several substack/investor-letter sources; the exact original primary source (which shareholder letter or interview) for the quoted sentence could not be independently pinned down in this environment. Treat as third_party and unverified as to the precise origin of the quote.

events.text: In August 2023 Constellation Software announced a 'warrant dividend' (declared August 16, 2023) and separately declared a dividend and filed a final prospectus in relation to a previously announced rights offering of Series 1 Debentures (August 24, 2023). These were non-cash special distributions (warrants / debentures) rather than a cash special dividend per share, so they are recorded here as events rather than under dividends_per_share_special.
events.source_title: Constellation Software Inc. Announces Declaration of Warrant Dividend

events.text: Foreign-exchange-adjusted organic net revenue growth (excluding US Healthcare businesses) was reported at approximately 4% in each of FY2015, FY2016, FY2017 and FY2018, per a third-party synthesis of Constellation's shareholder letters; the company has described its combined ROIC-plus-organic-growth metric as a proxy for the annual increase in shareholder value and reported keeping it at or above 30% for more than a decade.
events.source_title: A Better Combined Ratio - by Andy - bizalmanac
events.note: Qualitative/narrative corroboration for the roic_plus_organic_pct figures above; does not provide a full clean year-by-year numeric table for the entire 2006-2025 window.
